references.text: The same expression 'there was no king in Israel' is used to describe the lawless period during the judges
Repeats the formula 'In those days there was no king in Israel' which frames the narratives at the end of the book of Judges
Concludes the book of Judges with the same phrase that there was no king in Israel, and that everyone did what seemed right to them
Another Levite from Bethlehem in Judah who also travels to the hill country of Ephraim
Cohabiting wives (pilegsh) are mentioned in the patriarchal narratives as part of the family structure
Bethlehem in Judah is mentioned as a hometown, the same city that later becomes David's birthplace
